Game 1 for me:

DW Nightmist

Visionary

EOW Bunker

Golem Unity

vs.  Mad Bomber Blade on Advanced.  In the Tomb.  (bad move)

I had run Bomber normal not that long ago and was unimpressed, I've never had a phenomenal game against him, even on advanced it had been a wash.

Until today.  Wow, the man threw down.  we got Hasten Doom, Disruption 5 devices and Force Field in the first first two rounds, and we were really, really hurting when he flipped.  Then first card was. . . Consider the freaking Price of Victory.  Then Baron started destroying all his targets and Anubis starts crushing my heroes mercilessly.  Swinging Blades comes out right after DW Mist gets the Amulet out, and she redirects to live so it is her at 2hp, everyone else dead.  She redirects Baron's blast with 2 of her last three cards and luckily survives the round with a target and Force Field being played and Starshield Necklace in her hand, 7 cards under Baron.

Then EOW Bunker let's her draw Mistform, Vis destroys the shield and Nightmist plays the Necklace, Gunity lets her play mistform where she stays while Baron get's crushed by Shamise, the Challenge of Fire, Swinging Blades and Judgement of Anubis finishing him off.

So even in her DW form, Nightmist is still ridiculous, it just takes longer to get Mistbound and Mistform, and you can't really fuel the Amulet.

Another game in.  Drawn-out affair between Apostate and Visionary, Legacy, and Parse.  Once again in the Pike Industrial Complex.

A recurring issue with some 3-hero groups is too much support and sometimes a lack of damage capacity when you need it.  That's when you end up depending on those one-shot damage cards of Visionary and Legacy for some extra pop at the right time.  And Parse's ability to make damage irreducible is quite useful against relics when they pile up and protect each other.

Apostate was eventually flipped and holding out fairly well.  However, Legacy was established and was intercepting damage and using Next Evolution to avoid damage and keep the heroes in the game.

At this point the environment took an active part.  A pack of mutated lab rats put in an appearance.  In one round they chewed Visionary into incapacitation.  In the next round they got an additional damage bonus and proceeded to chew up relics and demons.  Which left Apostate vulnerable to Legacy and Parse to finish him off.

posts.cooked:
Nightmist, The Sentinels, and Fanatic just took on The Chairman in The Block.

Nightmist did an Oblivion on the first few underboss-thugs to show up, and The Sentinels weathered the all-hero damage pretty well.  After that Nightmist went into Mist Form while high HP hero and tanked retaliation damage from the Operative while Fanatic and The Sentinels kept pace with the underbosses and thugs.

Things got a little wild with the appearance of a Prison Break - which put all five underbosses into play by the end of the villain turn.  Fanatic countered with an End of Days, but that pulled Nightmist out of Mist Form and cleaned out whatever ongoings the heroes had, such as Sentinel Tactics.

With a short villain deck the heroes and The Chairman flipped the heroes changed tactics.  Nightmist Mistbound the villain deck once, and beyond that an Enboldened Writhe was checking the bottom of the villain deck every turn for the other Prison Break.  It was eventually found and discarded.

The environment had been relatively benign so far, but now had two Time-Crazed Prisoners in play and a 9-card trash pile.  They proceeded to obliterate the Operative's hit points over the next two rounds.  Nightmist went back into Mist Form right before they finished with the Operative and started on her.  The Environment then cleaned itself up with a Lock Down on the last card in its deck.

The heroes started on The Chairman himself with a vengeance after finishing off the crippled Operative.  A turn later Fanatic drew Wrathful Retribution and finished The Chairman off the round afterwards.

A solid team effort where each hero pulled their weight and made an important contribution to the victory.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Gloomweaver taken down in Insula Primalis by a support team; DW Nightmist, Argent Adept, and Omnitron-X

Hero team weakness early on was simply inflicting damage.  Nightmist handled the initial set of zombies, but after that Voodoo Pins accumulated on her and she soon couldn't keep a hand in play.  Heroes did a lot of healing as Gloomy's cultists and some zombies did limited damage - mainly due to OX having high HP and the right plating in play. 

Argent Adept built up songs and instruments and OX accumulated a component set.  Sarabande of Destruction kept the dinosaurs in check and OX was keeping the zombies in check.

The game turned once OX got a Defensive Blast card in play.  With a +1 damage bonus from the Adept OX played Flechettes and triggered a defensive blast that swept out the voodoo pins, cultists, and zombies that were active.  This allowed Nightmist to get back into action.  From there Gloomy's relics were rapidly trashed; either immediately by Argent Adept after coming into play, or detected by Nightmist on the top of Gloomy's deck and then TImeshifted to the trash by OX.

Standard quick fight involving Plague Rat vs. Bunker, Scholar, and Eternal Haka at Freedom Tower.

All the heroes infected early on - and two of them took the damage to remove Infected once Plague Rat flipped.  Scholar played support, tanked a bit, and generally just held on.  Bunker got Flak Gun, Omni-cannon, and Grenade Launcher out and then sat there in Turret Mode and pounded away.  Haka mainly used Taiha, but also played Ground Pound twice in order to reduce the damage taken somewhat.  Also noted that Punish The Weak is not that bad a card for Haka in this situation since it reduces damage being inflicted on other heroes while infected.

Heroes were down to 5-8 HP each when Plague Rat went down.  Lots of ongoings into play and the heroes were all infected again by then as well.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Scholar, Nightmist, and Parse vs Citizen Dawn on a Mobile Defense Platform.

Scholar played tank for most of the game with a Iron Form that shrugged off minor attacks thoughout the game.  He did Truth Seeker and other attacks as opportunity permitted amidst plays to keep his hand size built up.  MDF supplying a large quantity of harmless targets helped him out as well.  His team support cards mixed well with the other heroes, especially allowing Nightmist extra plays to get equipment out or cast additional spells.

Nightmist rolled out Master of Magic and the Necklace and then started casting Oblivion repeatedly to pound on non-hero targets.  Lost everything to THAT CARD, built it up again, did a Mist Fueled Recovery to get HP back up, and then back to Oblivion or Planar Banishment when Dawn started rolling out ongoings.  The Amulet was out by then as well and Dawn caught quite a bit of redirected damage.

Parse did a mixed support role.  She discovered early that a Aurora was on the bottom of Dawn's deck (and it was left there).  The other Aurora wiped out her Critical Multiplier cards.  Targetting Arrow on Dawn helped quite a bit in the late game running down of Dawn's HP - especially since Nightmist was using Elder Ring to boost damage even further. 

And I'd argue that Dawn's citizens helped the hero cause.  Initial citizens where Truth and Spring.  Initial villain card play was Dare blowing Truth away.  And the ongoing for bringing citizens back from the trash never made it into play.

Spite (Agent of Gloom) vs Eternal Haka, Omnitron-X, and The Scholar in The Final Wasteland

Game starts in Spiite's favor as he gets three drugs flipped before enough victims are in the Safe House to flip him.  And then he knocks the heroes around a bit more before they empty the Safe House back out.  Omnitron-X has some components out and thus is playing an extra on-going every turn for one drug to put back in his hand.  Haka is doing some damage, but taking punishment.  The Scholar is tanking, and helping out with some support cards.  But the tide seems to be running against the heroes and OX is about to go down.

And Spite simply got crushed after that point.

Between Scholar playing a card that stopped Spite from causing damage for a turn and Haka playing Ground Pound Spite spent four turns not touching the heroes.  He also was pretty inefficient at taking out victims since Potential Sidekick sat out there and gave the heroes extra cards repeatedly.  In that calm OX assembled a full component set and just chipped away at Spite while providing healing.  Haka played Haka of Battle to boost Taiha damage three times.  And Scholar eventually discarded a 19-card hand to set Spite up for the killing blow by Haka.

(Aside: Looking at the drugs in play I also think I could have kept Scholar in play indefinitely.  Two Flesh To Iron would soak Spite's attacks and he'd need an extra ongoing in play each turn for a drug to push back to his hand.  Incap plays from OX and Haka get him a draw and a card play to put the extra ongoing back out.  With Scholar's draw that would give him enough cards for the discards to keep both Flesh To Iron cards out.  Not a lot of extra space to kill Spite, but I think he'd eventually win out - especially with a card like Potential Sidekick out there helping him with additional card draws to help power an attack or build a LEE engine.)

La Capitan appears at the Pike Industrial Complex and is opposed by Golem Unity, Freedom Tempest, and Omnitron-X.

Crew pours out quickly as the heroes can't take the ship down quickly.  Battleforged adds to this by thumping lab rats in order to get more villain cards into play.  On the fllp-side some early bot plays by Unity (Champion Bot, Swift Bot, Turret Bot) take up damage otherwise aimed at heroes.

Tempest played an early Electrical Storm, but later had it stolen.  He also got Grevious Hailstorm and Cleansing Rain into use as well, plus his usual blasting one-shots.  He also used his default power to destroy cards sitting under La Capitan after she flipped.

Omnitron-X helped out with extra card plays for himself and the other heroes.  He also got the Ablative Plating out early and tanked a lot of shots from La Capitan and Trueshot as a result.  A few Defensive Blasts were triggered, and he also managed to build up a good component stack.

Bomber Blade attacks Legacy, Absolute Zero, and DW Expatriette in The Final Wasteland.

Blade rolls out on-goings and one shots instead of targets to charge his bombs.  By the time he does the heroes flip him.  On his flipped side his gets flabbergasted after he death rays Expatriette twice for no apparent effect (Thank you Flak Jacket twice over).

Legacy rolled out Inspiring Presence, Motivational Charge, and the Legacy Ring, after which he played a one-shot now and then and otherwise Galvanized and pummeled Baron Blade for extra damage.  He also had Danger Sense in play and soaked environment attacks multiple times.

Absolute Zero rolled out his modules in the first two turns and then used one shots and base power to alternately blast Baron Blade and heal.  He also got a very useful one shot in that stripped Baron Blade of Living Forcefield and Backlash Field.

DW Expatriette started the game with Tactical Shotgun in hand.  She used that until it was lost when Baron Blade flipped.  Added a Flak Jacket and also used Shock Rounds with it.  With the damage bonus Legacy was supplying she simply blasted Blade's HP down.  After Blade flipped she played an Assault Rifle and pinged away at Blade and the Wasteland monsters that had turned up.  When she lost the first Flak Jacket to Blade's attack she played a second one that was in hand.

The Wasteland Monsters were not that dangerous to the heroes. Legacy's Danger Sense avoided damage, Baron Blade was low or 2nd low HP multiple times, and the Snowman was attacking AZ without any net effect.

posts.cooked:
A near run in a contest I'd normally consider to generate a blowout.

Ambuscade in Insula Primalis vs. Mr Fixer, Expatriette, and Freedom Wraith.

Ambuscade starts with 2 Reactive Platings in play.  Cloaking Device came out by Round 3, and came out of the trash twice as well.  He stayed hidden and chipped away at the heroes while letting the dinos do the dirtly work of wearing the heroes down.  Then he started rolling out devices and pounding away directly.  Plus a late play of Charged Attacks - which actually proved to be his undoing.

The environment played a part from the beginning.  Enraged T-Rex in the first round, and the second T-Rex came out in Round 4.  Raptors, poisonous plant life, and the Volcano as well.  Constant damage to the heroes, as well as a distraction from trying to hurt Ambuscade's devices or him when the cloak was down. And Obsidian Fields building up and making cards like Driving Mantis useless.

Fixer was... Fixer.  Dual Crowbars and a style depending on what needed hammered on.  Some vital card plays as well.  Grease Gun, Salvage Yard, and Grease Gun again late to get the heroes a touch of breathing room.  Expatriette rolled out guns, some ammo, and just blasted away constantly - mainly with the Assault Rifle.  Unload got played and resulted in the use in a single turn of Pride, Assault Rifle, and Tactical Shotgun in order to sweep out some dinos and also take down three devices.  RPG never turned up, which would have been useful.

Wraith had what I consider an off game.  Just couldn't get equipment out that quickly or use it that effectively.  Base power (hit two targets for 1 melee) was used a lot more than I expected to.  Grappling Hook only came up once, no Impromptu Invention cards, no Throwing Knives, just mixes of her non-weapon and support equipment.

Last round came around with each hero at less than 4 HP (1, 2, and 4).  Ambuscade has about 20 HP left, Charged Attacks, and two Automated Turrets in play.  Two Obsidian Fields are adding to the fun.  Fixer does a few damage to Ambuscade and one of the turrets.  Expatriette plays Hollow points, and uses the Shotgun on Ambuscade since using the Assault Rifle would kill a Turret and trigger Charged Attacks to kill all three heroes.  Things are pretty grim. 

Wraith plays Inventory Barrage and blows up five pieces of equipment to take out most of Ambuscade's remaining points.  Base power hits Ambuscade for 3 points, and the second attack kills a damaged turret - which triggers Charged Attacks and is used to take out Ambuscade (and win the game).

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Randomly rolled Sentinels and Visionary against randomly rolled the Chairman and Silver Gulch; Legacy was picked deliberately because I absolutely refuse to play against the Chairman unless Legacy is involved. The Chairman’s first cards were Rook City Is Mine! and the Broker, which put a copy of Sustain the Portal and Sheriff Pratt into play. It wasn’t the worst possible set-up.

I wasn’t willing to play the top card of the villain deck just yet, so I didn’t play a card with Legacy and just Galvanized everyone. The Sentinels came up next and played Horrifying Dichotomy, prompting the Chairman to get a useless copy of Perfect Human Specimens before the Sentinels destroyed the Informant and got in four points of damage to the Operative, prompting Legacy to take a single point of retaliatory damage. Mainstay buffed the Sentinels, then Visionary, who had no useful cards, put out a copy of Psychic Maelstrom to beat down the Broker enough for Sheriff Pratt to almost definitely target and kill her during the environment phase and to hit the Operative for three more points. She used Enlighten on Legacy to try to get a copy of Lead From the Front out, since he already had Next Evolution and the Legacy Ring in his hand, but no luck.

A copy of Explosives Wagon came out on the environment phase; I groaned a little in anticipation of suckage to come but took consolation in watching Pratt kill the Broker for me. Legacy took two points of spiteful revenge. Another copy of Rook City Is Mine! came out, bringing out a Water Trough and Cyrus Hayes. The Muscle and the Enforcers followed, which I thought was pretty lucky, though it kind of broke my heart to discard Aura of Vision to keep the Idealist from taking 4 HP of damage from the Enforcers.

I weighed my options carefully and decided the best long-term strategy for survival was to play Next Evolution and immunize Legacy to melee damage, since Explosives Wagon was basically Galvanizing everyone for free anyway. The Sentinels played Unique Capabilities because I was pretty sure they were going to play Dark Delusions anyway, but it never hurts to have two extra cards in your hand before committing to that. I pinged the Underboss and the Thug so Cyrus and Pratt could do the wetwork for me, and hit the Operative for another 4 HP before buffing their armor again. Visionary had nothing useful to do again, so she tossed out a Mental Divergence just in case we needed an card to sacrifice to a Thief later and again failed to give Legacy a Lead From the Front.

I don’t honestly remember the next several turns in that kind of detail, and you probably don’t need the specifics anyway. Gunmen and Cover came out in roughly equal proportion, so they were effectively immune to all but the most concentrated attempts at damaging them and finished off the villain targets I’d softened up; Legacy got out his ring and his Motivational Charge so the heroes were only losing a little HP very slowly while he was more or less immunizing the team to the Operative’s counterattacks (I never did draw Danger Sense, go figure); the Sentinels were my primary damage-dealers, carefully wearing the villain targets for the environment targets while maintaining armor at all times; Visionary didn’t get many useful cards and did whatever seemed least stupid at the moment, mostly manipulating the environment and always trying to get Legacy the life-saving Lead From the Front. It didn’t come out until the neighborhood of round 8. By the time it came out, everyone’s HP was low enough that Writhe with his Caliginous Form was doing most of the party-shielding anyway. Visionary started getting Suggestion cards around round 6 I carefully stockpiled for later.

With the help from all the cowboys, I actually flipped the Chairman at the beginning of round four. The environment cards couldn’t help me against him, so the heroes focused carefully on him while still trying to leave henchmen for the environment to handle.

Probably my favorite moment in the game was round five, when Tyler Hayes was going to kill off the Explosives Wagon and I very cynically manipulated the damage distribution to be wipe out as many henchmen as possible, then attack the wagon to blow it up so the other cover cards would immunize the rest of my teams of gunslingers from the damage, and only after the damage buff was gone did I allow him to hit the heroes. They were limping along after that, but a steady stream of HP from Legacy and the Sentinels kept them limping rather than falling over while Decoy Projections kept Visionary alive a lot longer than she deserved to live and kept the Contract buried under the essentially useless Enforcers. He did come out eventually, but Visionary managed to keep the deck from shuffling with all those stockpiled Suggestion cards until after the Operative died.

I was on my game, but I don’t delude myself: it was at least fifty percent luck I won. Extremely lucky early draws from each and every deck and some very well-timed cards later in the game meant only the Idealist died from a bad combination of Tyler Hayes and the other Sustain the Portal (while Caliginous Form kept up a steady stream of ping-damage on the Chairman that would make him retaliate against his own henchmen and kill them, which I will never stop thinking is funny), but in the final round, with the Chairman at 1 HP, the Sentinels played Second Chance just to get her back…so she could zap him and end the game.

Matriarch waits her first turn with two Darken the Sky plays.  Heroes roll out some cards and work on both the Matriarch and the Mask.  Adept is using Scherzo of Frost and Cold, and Ra uses a Fire Blast and Pyre to finish off the Mask.  That leaves Young Legacy opportunity to hit the Matriarch and get Motivational Charge into play.  Police Backup arrives and shoots the Matriarch as well.

Matriarch rolls out 5 fowl and a damaging one-shot.  The Adept plays an instrument, and damages the Matriarch for a few points.  Ra does Inferno to hurt the Matriarch and take out the deployed fowl.  Ra and Legacy split the retaliation damage.  Ra Pyres the Matriarch as well.  Young Legacy plays The Legacy Ring and hits Matriarch with both Motivational Charge and Atomic Glare.

The Environment plays Plummeting Monorail.  The police shoot the Matriarch.

The Matriarch plays a Carrion Field.  (So the heroes get another turn without worrying about getting hurt.)

Adept gets Young Legacy a free play - and Inspiring Presence comes out.  Scherzo of Frost and Cold nows does 4 damage.  Ra plays Imbued Fire and all the hero damage gets another +1 damage.  He Pyres the Matriarch for 4 HP as well. 

From there the heroes (and the Environment) just pound away at the Matriarch.  Cohorts come out next, but it's too late by then as the heroes just ignore them and concentrate on taking the Matriarch herself out and have enough extra sacrificial ongoing cards to handle her one-shots that destroy them.

===

However, an interesting comparison in seeing the same hero, villain, and environment combination play out completely differently in back-to-back plays.

Chairman Pike and his Operative started off with a few Undivided Attentions, dealing a crapload of damage right out the gate.  After that it was relatively slow.  You had your typical 1 Underboss per round from Operative, which eventually brought out more thugs.  Both Prison breaks ended up being at the very bottom of the deck, so they came out one after another, AFTER all the underbosses had been killed.  So we suddenly had a LOT of targets out in play at once.  Other than that, nothing too abnormal happened with the villain deck.
 
Pike Industrial had some early game vat explosions help take out some thugs and underbosses.  Setback used Cash Out to heal some of the influx of damage from the explosions.  near the end of the game we got 2 Irradiated Cyclohexane Vats out boosting all damage by 2.  It was at that time that the Prison Breaks occured. We had rats coming out every so often up till that point, and they were all in the trash.  Then of course we got the experimental mutagens to bring out all the rats and boosting their damage, which ended up helping clear out the prison break. (at this point, we had around 14 non-hero targets in play) 
 
 
Setback applied a liberal use of Mitigate throughout the game and Cashed Out at opportune moments to provide healing to the rest of the team.  He really didn't draw the best combination of cards throughout the game, which was unfortunate.  He was the first to be incapacitated, which actually helped by allowing Ex-Pat and Fixer to use powers more often.
 
Ex-Pat was a steady stream of damage.  She got an assault rifle, speed loading, and 2 copies of hollowpoints early on. and a shotgun for single target hits.  This let her hit 3 targets per round for 4 damage (before other dmg+'s) which really helped keep thugs and underbosses out of play. She never really had much time to even use Aim.  She was incapacitated second, at which point Fixer was allowed to use bitter strike 3 times in one round (which ate up a LOT of equipment).
 
Mr Fixer used his wrench most of the game for the bonus to damage and defense, destroying styles with bitter strike.  He eventually got bloody knuckles, jackhandle, and alternating tiger claw  out all at the same time to deal a ton of irreducable to every non-hero target shortly after both prison breaks went off, to nearly clear the board.  He also got a really well timed Grease Gun out that kept Setback and Ex-pat alive for one extra turn so they could do more damage before dying. He was incapacitated last.
 
Nightmist was in and out of Mist form for most of the game.  with some lucky shuffling/draws, she seemed to always have it as an option.  Her biggest contribution was her amulet of elder gods, which allowed her to redirect some pretty nasty hits towards the Operative and later, the Chairman. Near the end, after the prison break and mutated rat swarm were dealt with by Fixer's amazing combo, she popped Mist-Fueled Recovery with 18+ cards in her discard to heal back up to full health.  
 
At this point all that was left on the board was Nightmist (at near full health), and the Chairman (at around 10 health).  She was preparing to nuke Pike utilizing her hand which comprised half her deck at this point, However, an unexpected second round of Mutated Rats poured out onto the field, devouring The Chairman and taking a sizable chunk out of Nightmist!
(Chairman is immune to environment damage, but since he was doomed at this point, I like to imagine that it ended this way)

I was resigned to failure nevertheless in the third game, but the first card he put out was a Good Samaritan, and Wraith’s Infrared Eyepiece put another Good Samaritan on top of his deck so that at the beginning of the second round, two victim cards were under the Safe House and his only drug card, the one that does damage whenever you use a power, was turned face-down again. With him unable to get any drugs turned up, the game was over in six rounds (Absolute Zero’s first played card was Impale, Bunker’s was Gatling Gun, Expatriette’s was Pride, and Wraith got out a Utility Belt and a Razor Ordinance in round two, so damage was plentiful). Everyone had at least 20 HP at the game’s end.

It bothers me that only an unlucky shuffle for Spite enabled me to beat him. I still haven’t figured out any reliable way to handle this jerk.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: I got tired of always going for the villain with the most rounds left to go, so I decided to tackle a villain I haven’t played in so long I wasn’t even sure I remembered how to fight her: Kismet. Randomly determined Team Leader Tachyon, Golem Unity, Dark Watch Setback, and Greatest Legacy fought her in the Mobile Defense Platform. Between Golem Unity and Dark Watch Setback, the heroes ended up doing way more damage to themselves than Kismet did. Unity got out her Stealth Bot in the second round, so between Bee Bots and “Whoops! Sorry!” cards, the only times she had enough jinx cards in play to boost her damage above what Stealth Bot would soak, Tachyon would punch her ability to do damage right off her. Over and done with in five rounds.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Dark Watch Setback, the Argent Adept, Freedom Tempest, and Greatest Legacy had a bit of a nailbiter (everyone’s in single HP), but ultimately they beat the crap out of Cosmitron. Took forever to get Tempest a card with a power that deals damage, but Cosmitron played Sedative Flechettes in his first round and Tempest put out Healing Downpour, so everyone stayed pretty high until the last Sedative Flechettes at the bottom of Cosmitron’s deck. Setback put out some fair tons of damage, though, and Tempest would get out a one-shot damaging card now and then, so all was well.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I really do hate Iron Legacy.

He decided to invade the Mobile Defense Platform, presumably to kill Baron Blade. Redeemer Fanatic, Visionary, Freedom Tempest, and Horus all tried to stop him. He had two damage buffs out in play from setup, an armor, and the one that gives him HP when heroes use a power. He proceeded to beat the everloving hell out of the team, inflicting at least ten points to everyone before his first card was played. Fanatic’s first play was Undaunted because she didn’t have anything better to do with her time (at least it would take care of that psychic damage); Visionary put out a Decoy Projection and tried to get Fanatic to draw an Apocalypse (didn’t happen); Tempest put out Vicious Cyclone, again for want of a better idea; Horus summoned and played his staff.

A mechanic came out of the environment deck.

Iron Legacy dealt seven more points of damage to everyone.

Fanatic threw out Divine Focus for want of anything useful to do and tried to draw Apocalypse (again, nope); Visionary had nothing to play and tried to give Fanatic an Apocalypse; Tempest dealt Iron Legacy three points from a Vicious Cyclone and five more from a Lightning Slash. Horus blasted Iron Legacy for five points, which would have flipped him, but by then I had an idea and used Horus’s power to heal Iron Legacy back up to 21.

Another mechanic came out of the environment deck.

Legacy killed Tempest and did everyone else another seven or so points of damage. Fanatic was down to 9 HP. She played Wrathful Retribution, knocking Legacy down to 2 HP. Visionary panicked and put up a Telekinetic Cocoon; Tempest rotted a bit; Horus played Imbued Flame and destroyed his staff for 5 HP, which even with Iron Legacy’s two points of healing was enough to wipe him out.

Three rounds. Yeesh.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Well, the Vengeance Five got their frigging vengeance, killing Dark Visionary, Expatriette, Redeemer Fanatic, and Freedom Tempest in the Final Wasteland. In the end, Ermine and X were the only ones left, and X was being fed a steady stream of HP while X’s Ablative Coating took care of any damage Ermine could inflict. posts.name: JimB

Engine of War Bunker was there to destroy her Diversions, Dark Watch Setback was there to do that as well as inflict damage, and Rook City Wraith was there to do pretty much everything at all times because she’s awesome like that but mostly to make sure Megalopolis didn’t screw us. Because of Wraith, two police officer cards were in play tearing Miss Information down when she flipped, and their efforts were appreciated even though the Gatling Gun, the Flak Cannon, the big dummy’s fists, and even the skinny chick’s throwing knives were all doing better jobs. posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I swear to god I love the frigging Sentinels.

Plague Rat went to the Final Wasteland to hunt down Chrono-Ranger, who was actually in the past hunting Plague Rat so they just missed each other. Instead, the rat found the Sentinels, Dark Visionary, Tachyon, and Engine of War Bunker. I was worried that the Sentinels wouldn’t last, but their constant teamwork (Sentinel Tactics and Hippocratic Oath both got out in the first round) ensured that they’d always be capable of both inflicting damage and healing. Dark Visionary was far and away the most important member of the team, though, using a combination of her base power, Precognition, and Suggestion to make sure Plague Rat only ever got to play useless ongoing cards that either she, Tachyon, or the Engine of War would destroy.* Tachyon was the biggest damage dealer due strictly to her late-game Lightspeed Barrages, but the Engine of War pounded away pretty hard first with a Flak Cannon, then with a Grenade Launcher when one would become relevant, and after round four with both thanks to a Turret Mode. posts.name: Azqa
posts.cooked: After two failed attempts to save The Dreamer from succumbing to whatever the Treacherous Ape is trying to get her to do (according to conversations elsewhere on this forum) in Megalopolis, the team of Parse, Absolute Zero, Setback, and the Scholar had better luck in the universe where the little girl was roused from slumber while on a tour of the Freedom Tower.  Sadly for Setback, he was in the wrong place at the wrong time when there were two Entry Points and a Dark Hero active and got overloaded with psychic damage, but that did allow Absolute Zero to take out the last two projections needed to save a young girl from her own nightmares.

posts.name: KainNived
posts.cooked:
After getting stomped into the ground by Iron Legacy a few times I decided to change tack and make myself feel better by beating up gloomy.

Seems a cult following for him had sprung up in The Block of all places.  Rook City Wraith, Dark Watch Expatriette, a time displaced and confused Engine of War Bunker, and Dark Watch Mister Fixer showed up to sort things out.

I initially thought it was going to be a real quick game as the Drum and Book pulled in the first rounds.  Set ups went fairly well for everyone but Bunker, couldn't pull any power cards so he mainly functioned as Dark Watch Mister Fixer's ammo tank.  After the first two relics dropped I got nervous that Vast Following would pull, so everyone started unloading on Gloomy.  Classic throwing knives, razor ordnance, micro on Wraith.  Shotty with speed loading and a hollow point/shock round rotation going on DW Expatriette.  Gattling Gun and Flak Cannon on Bunker.  Grease monkey fist and dual crowbars on Fixer... Holy crap can he lay down punishment like that if properly supported.  Bloody knuckles, overdrive, charge all saw use in the last few rounds too.

The pouch did pull eventually.  On the last round.  Gloomy only had 7 hp.  Buuut as Wraith could do 8 damage to it, and Expat 6, EoW 5, and Fixer could do 9 (charge, plus monkey and crowbars) I decided to go ahead and take the relic win...  Just cause.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Skinwalker Gloomweaver rose from one of the corpses in the morgue of the Block, but didn’t realize the pocket dimension would contain his newly corporeal form long enough for a group of heroes to mount an offensive. Fittingly, it was Fanatic who led the charge against the Qlippothic monstrosity; Dark Watch Mr. Fixer, the Sentinels, and Haka were all on hand to join the fight.

It was frigging grueling. Twenty-one bloody damned rounds, and I blame every last one of them on Dark Watch Mr. Fixer. Haka and Fanatic were both knocked down to the absolute minimum possible efficiency as each one had to spend at least one round in two crapping out some card to sacrifice to Bitter Strike; I exempted the Sentinels from this because they don’t have that many cards and needed every one they could pull. It took ten rounds to flip Gloomweaver, and would have taken longer if Fixer’s first card hadn’t been Riveting Crane Style, his second hadn’t been Jack Handle, and his third hadn’t been Harmony. His ability to hit all enemies simultaneously and knock any DR off them was key enough to compensate for how much he reduced Fanatic and Haka to a crawl. The round before Gloomweaver flipped, Fanatic got out her Zealous Offense, which put an even greater burden on Haka to be the one to sacrifice his cards to Mr. Fixer’s blind rage since she couldn’t afford to lose Absolution or Zealous Offense if she wanted to keep Gloomweaver from destroying everyone, but he got by, and Fanatic eventually started getting out a few cards here and there to help; a Sacrosanct Martyr, an Undaunted, whatever.

The Sentinels were the steadiest source of damage, but they didn’t get out Sentinel Tactics until he’d flipped, so a lot of their early damage was stunted by being required to spend their power phase on Mainstay armoring them all. Haka got out a Taiaha fairly early and didn’t have to sacrifice it until he got a spare in his hand, so he was reliably inflicting three points of damage to two targets pretty much all the time.

The inmates in the Block never inflicted any damage. They were either destroyed by a Jack Handle as soon as they got into play, were shot down by agents, or were prevented form inflicting damage by the various cards in the hero decks that prevent bad guys from doing damage.

At the end of the game, thanks to an early play of Hippocratic Oath, the Sentinels were all at max HP, and the rest of the team was in the high teens, save of course for Fanatic, who’d been spamming Sacrosanct Martyr to inflict maximum damage on the zombie-god. I like to think that holy light shattered his spirit beyond reconstruction, but he’s a villain and they seem to have Get Out Of Oblivion Free passes, so probably not.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Setback, the Scholar, Expatriette, and Tempest all got shockingly lucky against Cosmitron in Freedom Tower. I was sure I was gonna die in round three when both Electro-whatever gates came out, but concentrated pouring-on of damage knocked it down to only sixteen HP of damage to everyone, and by then the Scholar had Mortal Form to Energy in play, Tempest had Cleansing Downpour, and Setback had no offense but three cards in hand that would heal the entire party; so everyone was healing back 4 HP per round for three rounds (more when the Scholar got out that one that heals everyone). I was actually being real careful not to inflict too much damage on Cosmitron himself because the only components he had in play were those wussy railguns and I was happier with them in play than a potential army of frigging drones as might happen if he flipped.

Around round ten, the Freedom Tower card that deals everyone 2 HP of cold came out just after Setback had put out the one that lets him absorb and/or redirect damage dealt to other heroes, and he had a good store of unlucky tokens stockpiled, so Cosmitron was taking 8 HP per round from that card (by my reading, Setback still has to suffer damage that targets him and he can’t redirect that; am I wrong?). That helped a lot. Setback was down to 3 HP at the end, but everyone else was at least in the teens when Expatriette played her final Unload with a shotgun, an Uzi, a pistol, and some flaming ammo in one of them to blow the robot apart once and for all.

With Cosmitron reduced to so much crackling rubble, the heroes then all went to find Unity and kick her ass for her, because her Playground came into play and turned all ongoing cards into equipment cards exactly before Cosmitron destroyed all equipment cards. It wasn’t really her fault, but it wasn’t really not her fault either, so I don’t want to hear anyone complaining about fairness.

Completely unrelated to the game I just played, I wonder if the upcoming character Captain Cosmic’s nemesis will be the currently unnamed jerk who decided to power up Cosmitron.

One should never be surprised when they run into The Ennead at The Tomb of Anubis.  Least of all the paranormal investigator Faye Diamond, the Dark Watch member known as Nightmist.  She was however surprised when the ritual performed by the Ennead tore open a hole in the fabric of spacetime and she recieved help from those thrilling heroes of yesteryear America's Greatest Legacy and G.I. Bunker!

The only members of the Ennead that made it out to play were Nephthys, Geb, and Tefnut, none of the others got a chance to come out to play.  Bunker got his grenade launcher out early, and with Greatest Legacy's support he was able to lob a ridiculous amount of grenades at the egyptians.  Throw in some inspiration, the flak cannon, and turret mode and the vintage artillery fell like rain. 

DW Nightmist meanwhile managed to play lockdown on the villain deck, while they did get a few cards out they never got another of their ilk out to play. 

The environment helped out as well dropping several trials that beat the Ennead as badly as the heroes.   In the final environment turn The Lord of the Underworld Anubis made his grand entrance, just in time to collect Nephthys personally when G.I. Bunker Flak Cannoned her to death.

The heroes never didn't get to recover any artifacts, none the less Faye considered the expedidtion a success.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Wanting to finish off the Scholar just because seeing those black lines makes me feel as if we’re progressing, I threw him against the Chairman when a thought occurred to me: when I started playing this game, I only played three characters at a time because that’s all my space can afford. It wasn’t until I decided to start wiping Vengeance Five games off the map that I cleared a big ol’ space off the living room floor, arranged things in a circle around me, and hunkered down in the center. Now that I know I have room for five heroes, why not try five heroes against the Chairman, since almost nothing in his deck scales with hero numbers, and see if that doesn’t work?

Well, it worked. It worked fast. Six rounds and he was down, after flipping at the start of the third. Team Leader Tachyon kept everyone drowning in cards; Unity was lucky enough to get out Swift Bot and a Platform Bot in the first round; Freedom Tempest had roughly two third of his deck in hand at the end of the game when his first play was Localized Hurricane that just wiped out the mooks; Absolute Zero almost didn’t even have time to get his setup in play but did manage to Impale the Operative in the first round; and the Scholar…well, actually, the Scholar didn’t have anything to do. The Chairman’s first card was “Rook City Is Mine!” which put Mission Control in play, so since the Scholar had no good cards in hand his first play was Know When to Hold Fast, and then Mission Control put Know When to Turn Loose into play. I didn’t mind hitting the Operative for 9 HP, but it sucked not having any cards in his hand.

Oh, well. The Chairman learned a valuable lesson about trying to acquire superhero real estate when they’re home and have something to say about it.

posts.name: KainNived
posts.cooked:
While reading a weathered copy of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire in the far off wastes of the far future the Eternal Haka was surprised to find a time rift opening in front of him. It had been decades since the last one. He considered it good to take a walk about in the time stream now and again, one gets to be around people again, a chance to see old friends possibly, pick up some more books, and maybe even a cupcake if the time was right. Thus he walked through the time portal to find himself on an old familiar battle ground sadly bereft of cupcakes. The pike industrial complex, where he heard a villain monologuing.

It was Kismet, standing across from her ready for battle were two members of Darkwatch, Nightmist and Expatriette, as well as Rook City’s own Wraith! One would have thought the villainess’s unnatural luck would have kept an additional opponant away, but time has a way of evening out luck. Perhaps that’s why it had to come from so far.

Things went pretty simply. Set ups were fast. Expat had Pride in the starting hand and quick draw so she was able to bring the heat. Haka also therw down punishment and managed to keep himself healed. Wraith played deck manipulation which kept Kismet in check and kept the rats from mutating. DW Nightmist was able with the neckless and deck stacking to keep blasting Kismet’s ongoings and occasionally deal damage while healing herself.

That just leaves 4 base set heroes left to face Kismet! So by all means someone take her out!

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Because I am arrogant and stupid, I wanted to get as many slots cleared off as I could. Only six heroes left hadn’t fought any of the Vengeance Five yet, so of them I picked Engine of War Bunker, KNYFE, Dark Watch Mister Fixer, the Sentinels, and Dark Watch Setback (the last choice was agonizing, but between him and Parse, I figured I needed more HP to soak up the hits). The five of them boarded the Mobile Defense Platform, figuring it would just be Baron Blade pulling his usual Bizarro-Murphy-from-Sealab-2021 shtick,* but instead there was a bloody damned army of villains in there that the team was, frankly, woefully unprepared for. The Engine of War was pretty useless; after destroying a couple of enemy ongoings, he didn’t get a weapon car in hand for almost six rounds and was lucky to get a few External Combustions he could use. KNYFE was slightly better, though her first two cards were party-damaging Incidental Contacts because she too couldn’t get any equipment in hand until the end of round two. Mister Fixer tried to keep putting his own style cards in play to sacrifice for punches, but he did end up having to dip into Bunker’s Ammo Drop for the sake of keeping his own Dual Crowbars in play; the Sentinels were, as usual, MVPs with a fairly early play of Sentinel Tactics combined with some lucky draws of their various “damage everyone, or at least more than one person” cards to keep them going at a good clip. Dark Watch Setback contributed slightly more than the Engine of War did, mostly by putting out useless ongoings to sacrifice to either Mister Fixer or Ermine (whom I will hate forever), though he did get off some very well-timed Exceeded Expectations to wipe out his unlucky pool before playing a previously suicidal Cause and Effect.

The Vengeance Five were screwed by, paradoxically, a lucky draw. At the start of round one, Baron Blade helped Proletariat get four clones into play, so of course the heroes pounded on him as hard as they could to make sure he’d finish himself off in round two with his own psychic damage. He put out ten HP of damage in round one, but killed himself off in round two. After that, it was a matter of focusing on whoever was screwing the group more (looking at you, Revenant) or whose death would screw the party least (looking at you, Ermine), and just hoping to get good cards in hand.

Around round six, Writhe was the hero with the most HP left (he had 13) and I finally got Caliginous Form into play, nearly immunizing the entire party from damage. Since everyone else had in the neighborhood of six to eight, that was extremely important. In round nine, the villains were defeated. I’d been delaying killing Friction for as long as possible because when Dark Watch Mister Fixer is in your group, you don’t need anyone’s help wiping out the party’s setup, so a final play of Horrifying Dichotomy wiped her and the Baron out in a single blow.

Sparks: Why would we want to blow up the Earth, where we are right now?
Bizarro Murphy: Because it is…BIZARRO!
Sparks: It’s STUPID.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Baron Blade, Friction, Fright Train, and Proletariat got together in Rook City to try to free their pal Ermine from state prison where she was serving time for being a generally awful person. posts.cooked:
My god. I think I’m done with this game for a while.

Grand Warlord Voss in the randomly chosen Tomb of Anubis vs. more or less randomly chosen Price of Freedom Wraith, Eternal Haka, Bunker, and Nightmist. Voss’s setup cards are one Gene-Bound Frosthound, two Gene-Bound Psi-Weavers, and one Gene-Bound Shock Infantry; his first draw is TCF Conqueror. First round, every hero has taken at least 9 HP.

Wraith plays Throwing Knives and plinks away. Haka plays Ground Pound, thank god. Bunker plays Grenade Launcher and plinks away, finishing off a Psi-Weaver. Nightmist has nothing good in her hand, so she plays Heedless Lash and puts Mist Form into play, which she just does to have something to sacrifice to the warship. Luck of luck, one of the two cards she draws is her Amulet of the Elder Gods.

Shamise comes out of the environment. “Okay,” I think, “I can deal with this.”

Playing two cards because of his warship, Voss plays a Gene-Bound Guard and Field Lieutenant Tamar. All villain targets save for the warship have DR 2; Wraith and Bunker cannot hurt them. I begin to cry very softly to myself, but carrying on is really my only choice, so Wraith plays a Utility Belt to inflict two whole points of damage to Shamise. Haka plays Taiaha and knocks Shamise for three, then the Gene-Bound Guard for one. Bunker plays his Gatling Gun and inflicts one whole point of damage to the warship and two to Shamise, finishing him off. Wraith takes the Rod of Anubis for the sake of having something to hit with. Nightmist plays her Amulet, then damages herself with Investigation for the sake of bouncing it back as one point of damage to the Guard.

Judgement of Anubis comes out, hurting the whole team but luckily finishing off that damned guard so one point of the two points of damage can leak through to the minions. There’s no stopping the hail of damage coming out, though, and Wraith loses her Utility Belt. Everyone is down to about 11 HP.

Wraith has zero effective damage potential, so she plays Infrared Eyepiece to at least bury one more Gene-bound Guard. The minions have to go, so the party grits their teeth and take it as Haka plays Rampage, wiping out the minions and taking a lot of punishment from Anubis for it. His Taiaha finishes off the lieutenant and takes a chunk out of Anubis, though a bit late. Bunker focuses fire on the warship, finally killing it, and getting out some Heavy Plating a bit late to be useful. Nightmist plays another Heedless Lash and bounces the damage at Anubis, and putting a useless Scouring Mists into her hand.

A Swarm of Scarabs come out and I curse every known deity, then make a few up to curse them too. Voss flips and gets a Forced Deployment because of course he does. Wraith tosses out another Utility Belt and starts chucking knives and zapping Voss for an overwhelming three HP. Haka puts out Ta Moko and finishes off Anubis, then wallops Voss, who is not amused. Bunker shoots the alien warlord twice, plays Auxiliary Power Source because what else is he doing with these cards, and passes to Nightmist, who plays Planar Banishment to get rid of the Swinging Blades and the Forced Deployment. A few tons of minions come out, none of whom Nightmist is capable of damaging any longer, so she draws her card and hopes for the best.

Mdjai comes out to ping all the heroes, which annoys me.

When Voss’s turn comes, the damage Nightmist inflicted to herself with her early spells is enough that the rush of minions wipe her out. The rest of the group is anywhere between four and one HP. It seems like game over, but I am stubborn, and I have an ace up my sleeve: Wraith’s Smoke Bombs. Almost any damage anyone would inflict should be reduced to nothing by them. She has nothing useful to do now, so she halfheartedly zaps Mdjai with the Rod of Anubis and peeks at Voss’s deck. Haka plays Punish the Weak and can now inflict three points of damage to a minion, which he uses to wipe out the Gene-Bound Guard first and that Gene-Bound Shock Infantry Next. Bunker shoots as many people as he can. Nightmist’s ghost uses some mojo to heal Wraith up to 2 HP in case something happens.

It carries on like that for four more rounds, with damage being diverted to armored targets and reduced down to nothing so the whole group is at no higher than 4 HP at any time. Wraith gets out a Stun Gun eventually but can’t penetrate Voss’s armor for two rounds until she finally gets a Micro-Targeting Computer and can stun him to the point that he can no longer damage anyone very much and Nightmist’s ghost keeps healing as best she can. In the final round, Voss pulls out another Forced Deployment and, with 24 HP left, that’s pretty much game over. It is not physically possible to deal that much damage with the cards I have, so all I can do is play and hope for the best.

Wraith plays a second Infrared Eyepiece because there’s nothing else to do. This brings her up to eight pieces of equipment in play. She hits Voss for 6 HP with a Throwing Knife and a Stun Gun, and draws an Inventory Barrage.

One of Nightmist’s incapacitated powers is to allow a player to play a card. If Wraith plays that, she’ll inflict up to 16 points of damage. Haka only needs to hit for 2 to finish the game.

So, with Wraith at 1 HP, Haka at 4, and Bunker at 2, the heroes manage to kick the alien out of the Tomb of Anubis.

I should feel exhilarated, and maybe I will tomorrow, but for right now? Yeah, enough is enough.

posts.cooked: Advanced Ambuscade against Dark Watch Mister Fixer, Greatest Legacy, KNYFE, and Tempest in Freedom Plaza was over in about eight rounds, even though Legacy was immunizing the group against projectile damage by round 3. As usual, Mister Fixer was the biggest stumbling point, delaying everyone’s growth with his Bitter Strike. There were three rounds of unmitigated fire damage from his grenade launcher or whatever that card is called, but everything got beat down pretty rapidly.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Wraith, Mister Fixer, and Bunker against Miss Information in Silver Gulch. Her first diversion is “Diplomatic” Envoy and her first draw is Misplaced Memo, so the Envoy is immune to damage and I’ll lose at least one card if I play anything. Fine. I play Wraith’s Stun Bolt because it doesn’t have to inflict damage to reduce damage; Mister Fixer plays Mediation to get out Driving Mantis so at least he can redirect some of that critter’s damage; Bunker puts out Recharge Mode for the cards and so he’ll have something to sacrifice to Miss Information.

“I’m doing fine,” I reassure myself.

The environment deck plays a Prickly Cactus. “Good,” I say to myself, “now I can take down that Envoy card.”

Miss Information kills Bunker’s Recharge Mode and plays “Cat” Stuck in a Tree. I groan, but whatever. Mister Fixer bounces a point of damage back to the Envoy and takes 3 HP because there’s nothing he can do about it.

Another round goes by, everyone’s inflicting damage as best they can…then the environment screws everything with an Explosives Wagon. Suddenly, the only defense the team had–Mister Fixer catching the first hit and sending it back–is worthless, because every damage instance is above 3 and Mister Fixer can only draw style cards and Bloody Knuckles.

Mister Fixer goes down first. The Wraith follows. Enemies keep getting immunized from damage by that damnable Misplaced Memo, which I never have the time to destroy because everything else–a Suspicious Malfunction, a What Doesn’t Kill You–is more dangerous and needs to go first. Wraith’s final act was self-sacrifice; with 1 HP left, anything she did would have killed her, so she played Inventory Barrage to inflict 9 HP to the 10-HP Miss Information. Mister Fixer killed off Misplaced Memo, and Bunker took her out.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Dark Watch Expatriette, the Wraith, Young Legacy, and Horus versus Spite in Rook City because of course it would roll Rook City. With four heroes in play, I wasn’t really worried, especially after discovering Young Legacy had her party-immunity setup in hand before play, so it was mostly just a matter of praying he didn’t draw that one PL531 Compound Upsilon before round 3.

He didn’t.

Horus, however, did get a Burning Tornado out, and Wraith’s plays were, in order, Razor Ordinance, Micro Targeting Computer, Trust Fund, and Impromptu Invention + Utility Belt + Infrared Eyepiece.

Yeah, Spite never really had a chance.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: The Visionary, Haka, and Horus just whupped the Matriarch in the Block. I gotta say, she’s kind of a pushover if you have a single high-HP dude with a point of armor to eat all the damage. I never once felt bad about Visionary’s Demoralization…though to be fair, that’s because I destroyed her mask before her second Carrion Fields came out, and the second Carrion Fields was the first and therefore only card drawn on her turn that round. I rested a lot easier when Visionary put that newly-destroyed mask at the bottom of Matriarch’s deck.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Pretty straightforward game of Dark Watch Mister Fixer, GI Bunker, Fanatic, and Nightmist against Omnitron on the Mobile Defense Platfrom (I assume he was trying to cannibalize the technology). Not much to see except a bunch of dudes whaling on a robot, or occasionally a winged dude dropping much smaller robots onto the big one’s head, which is probably not as funny as I think it is but I still laugh. The best moment was when an Electro-Pulse Explosive came into play after Nightmist had her Amulet of the Elder Gods out, so everyone got to safely ignore it and just let her kill it with its own damage. Hee.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Team Leader Tachyon, Young Legacy, Freedom Tempest, and Golem Unity went up against Advanced Gloomweaver in the Final Wasteland (that last combination of two sounds familiar) and whupped him with depressing ease. Thanks in part to Tachyon, it only took Young Legacy three rounds to get out a Motivational Charge and a Legacy’s Ring, so she was healing everyone, punching whatever seemed squishy, and healing everyone every round. At the end of the game, the team was only down by a total of 6 HP.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Two games involving Dark Watch Mister Fixer, Absolute Zero (god do I prefer him to the Elemental Wrath version), Visionary, and Nightmist against Agent of Gloom Spite in the Block. The first one was a massacre. Spite’s first victim card was a Good Samaritan, and by a freak of chance, every time we let him play the top card of his deck to put the Good Samaritan in the Safe House, he drew a card that destroyed a victim–bye-bye, Good Samaritan–and put another in play…and of course it was another Good Samaritan that got destroyed while trying to put him in the Safe House by a card that put yet a third one in play, that then got destroyed by that one ongoing effect of his. Between that and his first drug being the one that deals damage if you use a power, it was impossible to catch up with either the drugs or his HP, and it was over in round 5.

The second attempt was much smoother. Everyone was fine. Nightmist did way more damage to the team than Spite did.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Greatest Legacy, Dark Watch Setback, Dark Visionary, and KNYFE against Bomber Blade in the Ruins of Atlantis. Dark Visionary kept Blade crippled by burying his good cards, Legacy made sure KNYFE was hitting often, and Setback got lucky enough to draw Looking Up in his opening hand so he could participate in the game. It was pretty much a matter of making sure Blade’s HP were the lowest so the Kraken, which everyone knew was coming because Visionary checked with her Prophetic Vision, would deal with him for us.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Redeemer Fanatic, Dark Watch Expatriette, GI Bunker, and the Argent Adept took on Baron Blade in the Mobile Defense Platform (heh), and boy I’m glad I had four of them, because it was a nail-biter to get him flipped before he destroyed the planet Earth. Expatriette did her best to keep the damage going on, but Fanatic really wasn’t pulling her own weight for the first five rounds while we waited for Absolution to get into play. Everyone eventually succeeded, though, and I never even got to bring out the big guns (rimshot) of an Unload, a Turret Mode, a Wrathful Retribution, whatever.

The environment was completely toothless. I didn’t even draw a damaging effect.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Fanatic, Mister Fixer (oh thank god for once it wasn’t Dark Watch), and Dark Watch Expatriette just fought the Matriach in Silver Gulch. Mister Fixer got out a Pipe Wrench in the first play and Expatriette got out a Submachine Gun, so really, nothing worth talking about happened. It was all just a matter of deciding whether Fanatic and Mister Fixer would be hitting a Carrion Field and/or a cohort while Expatriette made every bird that entered the field useless.

I did have a pretty hilarious mental image of an angel, an ancient sifu, and a cyclops with every kind of gun in hand all desperately whaling on the dirt of a Carrion Field until it stopped being evil (as indicated by a ring of stars circling over what counts as the dirt’s head), but yeah, it was all just pounding HP and letting the Matriarch be completely ineffectual against the team with her counterattacks.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Team Leader Tachyon, Rook City Wraith, and Bunker: EOW are called to Wagner Mars Base to deal with "ghosts".  There they find the phenomena is due to a young child.  Combat against The Dreamer's projections begins!

Early rounds are projections coming out faster than the heroes can stop them since no one has a base damage power and are not getting good early draws.  However, they get some equipment built up* and deal with the initial group of projections before too much damage is done.  Wraith's default power has been used repeatedly essentially to discard a number of environment cards due to limited attack options.  TLT's default power has been useful for making up for the damned Tooth Fairy projections.

The flip side battle is relatively short since only six projections need to be killed for the win.  This is slowed for a round by The Dreamer not playing any projections for three villain deck draws in a row.  A Meteor Storm helps the heroes by preventing projections and The Dreamer from doing any damage for a turn as well.  Both Whipacorns appear late in order to delay the inevitable.  The game ends on a Macabre Spectre attack (supported by Villainous Weaponry) being deflected back on it by TLT.

* - This group is relatively unaffected by The Dreamers flip since it destroys on-going cards and not equipment.  One Red Dust came up early, and Wraith caused the other to be discarded.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Expatriette and Setback (in Dark Watch mode) figure on taking a few days off in the Greek Isles.  Things go wrong quickly as an earthquake reveals the Ruins of Atlantis, a bunch of Egyptian gods arrive to loot the place, and Haka turns up looking to have "fun".

What proceeded was an endurance contest.  Haka's early play of Ta Moko proved key since he avoided a lot of the Ennead 1-damage attacks, and also took less damage when the attacks were assisted by the environment deck.  Atlantis rolled out a Kraken tentacle early, as well as Mystical Defenses, and both the Ennead and the heroes were getting pounded on.  Lucky for the heroes Shu did not come at as the Ennead got reinforced and soon has six opposed to the three heroes.  Some early equipment destruction slowed the heroes.  Haka rampaged twice to weaken the Ennead.  Expatriette got the SMG out and fed it hollow-point or incendiary ammo consistently.  Setback had issues getting an Unlucky Pool started, so he destroyed annoying environment cards (Toxic Seaweed!) until Looking Up eventually appeared.

Late in the game as the Ennead started dropping, so did Expat and Setback to a reinforced Ennead one-shot (each took 2 cold, 2 fire, and 4 lightning damage) from a 1+1+1 one-shot that was bonused by a Phosphorent Chamber and a Water Leak.  Haka rode it out, and then got benefit from getting Taiaha out and getting to use it repeatedly in a round due to the incap turns.  At that point he essentially beat the remaining weakened Ennead into the dust over the next two rounds.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Kismet (advanced) finished off by Legacy, Ra, Tempest, and Visionary in The Block. 

Too much hero firepower for Kismet to deal with.  Lady Luck and Inconceivable Obstruction slowed things for a bit, but Visionary eventually destroyed them.  Legacy had Inspired Presence going, did a Motivational Charge every so often, and got a key Heroic Interception in play.  Ra got his Staff out, played Imbued Fire, and then pretty much rolled out one-shots (Scorched Earth) and did Pyre shots at Kismet.  Tempest had Resilience and the Shackles out, plus Electrical Storm while doing Squall on most turns for considerable damage to the environment targets.  While not going after Kismet's ongoings Visionary had Demoralization going, and tossed out Decoy and one-shots as needed.   By the later rounds the Talisman was bouncing across and back every round from all non-hero targets damage from Tempest and Visionary.  (Though a one-shot by Kismet got Ra to shoot Visionary for 5 fire damage once - which did destroy a jinx card as well.)  The Block didn't do much.  Inconceivable Obstruction and Prison Riot got more environment targets into play - but either a Kismet one-shot or the Tempest/Visionary blitz would clear them out about as fast as they accumulated.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Alien grudge match in the Freedom Tower! Grand Warlord Voss tried to lead an entire army into a single skyscraper to get Tempest, and it didn’t really work out for him. Legacy, Expatriette, and Horus were on hand to repel the invasion, and, well, when Legacy gets out Inspiring Presence in the first round and Expatriette gets out Hairtrigger Reflexes in the second, that’s basically it. It’s over. His minions died as soon as they came out, leaving the Punisher, the Human Torch, and Storm to just pound on him until it was all over while Superman made sure Voss was hitting him with a damage type he was immune to, not that the last had much of a chance to matter. Five rounds and out.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I don’t know why the Dreamer, Freedom Tempest, Dark Watch Expatriette, and Dark Watch Setback were all in the Mobile Defense Platform. Maybe they weren’t. Maybe none of it happened. Maybe it was all just a dream sequence. Psychics, amirite?

Anyway, Tempest wasn’t as useless as you’d expect him to be, starting off with a strong draw and getting more single-target one-shots in hand than I’d have bet on. Dark Watch Setback was pretty much just there to destroy environment cards. The heavy lifting was up to Expatriette, but turns out that between an Assault Rifle and a Tactical Shotgun, she was pretty much up to the task. All the projections were destroyed in fairly short order, and then Link climbed the mountain to play the Ballad of the Wind Fish on the eight divine instruments, or whatever.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: GI Bunker, Ra, the Argent Adept, and Setback took on la Capitan in the Realm of Discord. It was a long game, but one of the easiest bouts against her I’ve ever had, assisted by lucky draws or, in the case of Setback’s Fumbling Fool, lucky discards; la Capitan only got to play a single one-shot that stole equipment and/or ongoings. It was just a matter of wearing her down and making sure there were plenty of cards for her to steal so she couldn’t have Bunker’s Turret Mode setup of Flak Cannon and Grenade Launcher.

posts.name: Bas
posts.cooked: Hej! Just finished a game in which TL Tachyon, DW Mr. Fixer, K.N.Y.F.E. and DW Setback took on Akash'Bhuta on Insula Primalis. Started off quite smooth with Tachyon, Fixer and KNYFE dealing nice bits of damage to Akash'Bhuta, who herself only put Brambles and Entombs out, and Setback taking some Friendly fire to build up his pool, being in the Wrong place most of the time, Mitigating incoming damage and Cashing out to heal the team. Luckily AB kept discarding Primordial plant life in favor of Raptor packs that were happy chewing on her appendages. However,things became ugly when AB flipped and DW Fixer decided to Jack Handle a row of appendages and dinosaurs to allow AB to heal all her appendages, destroy all hero ongoings and ruin everybody's day. Setback repeating this a turn later did not help, although him returning to Cashing out and Mitigating damage kept the team barely alive until his team-members could finish AB off to save the day.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
Citizen Dawn decided to set up her nation on Mars, which I have to admit would not have bothered me. Screw those guys; let them have Mars, for all I care, if it gets them out of my hair. Unfortunately, they decided to take over the Wagner Base, which is not theirs to take, and it offends me to see thieves get away with their prize, so the Sentinels, Horus, Dark Watch Nightmist, and Golem Unity were dispatched to take care of the problem; the Sentinels and Golem Unity were sent on the principle that if the heroes are facing down a nation of super-beings, the heroes should probably try to match the enemies in numbers, heh.

Citizen Dawn had only begun ferrying her subjects up. Citizens Anvil, Battery, Hammer, and Tears were there when the heroes arrived. Doctor Medico and Writhe beat the stupid out of Citizen Hammer and put a hurting on Citizen Tears so Horus could finish her off with a Living Conflagration, then accepted Mainstay’s armoring; Nightmist didn’t have any good spells prepared or relics in hand, so she took a moment to remind herself she’s a Master of Magic; Unity cannibalized a seemingly useless pylon to put out Speed Bot and Champion Bot, but that turned out to be a bad idea because that pylon set the biosphere on fire.

Citizen Autumn ferried herself to Mars. No one cared, though the Sentinels were slightly miffed it meant they couldn’t work at full potential. The heroes focused on beating up Citizen Battery, then went about whupping Citizen Dawn. By round three, Unity had out Speed Bot, Champion Bot, Stealth Bot, Raptor Bot, and usually a Bee Bot as well, so she was really tearing Dawn up, and Dawn was too dumb to stop aiming at Nightmist when the bigger problem had metal teeth latched into her femoral artery, though maybe that’s unfair of me; maybe she was woozy and confused from blood loss. To emphasize the point, Unity put out a Platform Bot and another Raptor Bot, so she was suddenly and reliably inflicting 20 HP per round. Citizen Dawn did not last long once the other Raptor Bot got her other thigh.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
I don’t know what Geb, Tefnut, and Nephthys were doing on the Mobile Defense Platform. I have no idea why they would ever even be there. Engine of War Bunker, Setback, and Dark Visionary were involved, though, so chances are the last two of them had something to do with it.

Setback and Visionary whupped on the bad guys as best they could, while Bunker kept yelling, “My guns won’t initialize! Nothing’s working! I need to try an Auxiliary Power Source! Hang on!” Visionary kept giving Setback suspicious looks he missed because he was busy whimpering and dancing like a monkey in a fez away from all the bursts of fire and magic and whatnot that the Ennead (and, occasionally, Baron Blade’s guards, who I guess just obey whatever order is given to them by any tosser with an evil smirk who wears a costume) kept trying to aim at the heroes but somehow always got aimed at Setback before hitting one of their own.

Geb and Nephthys were down, and Bunker had finally been able to initialize his Omni-Cannon, albeit to minimal effect. Visionary glared at Setback and said, “I don’t know how, but this is your fault. Bunker’s guns, the Ennead, all of it.”

“What? No it isn’t oh my god duck!” he yelled as Set came out of the elevator, hucking lightning at everyone. Nuit was behind him, surrounding the Ennead in an unearthly glow bullets bounced off of.

“So your fault,” Visionary muttered.

“So not!” Setback yelled back.

“Are you guys talking? I can’t hear anything! My head is under several inches of metal!” Bunker yelled.

Everyone focused fire on Nuit for a little bit and put her down at the exact moment Atum came up from downstairs.

“How are you even–I don’t get how you make these things happen!” Visionary complained, planting a palm square in the back of Setback’s head for emphasis.

“I am so totally not doing it! Also, ow!” Setback whined back, his tone perhaps justifiable given that he’d been perforated quite a bit in the last fight and his regeneration wasn’t really keeping up with it.

“What?” Bunker yelled.

Atum coughed, embarrassed. “Um, are we going to fight here, or do you guys need a minute?”

“Oh, shut up,” Visionary groused, and stuck invisible fingers into Atum’s brain before wrapping herself in a cocoon of pink energy that drew all of Atum’s flames and unholy power toward her, then bounced it back at him. He burned quite nicely. A few of Blade’s goons came out with marshmallows and hotdogs just in time to see Bunker, whose Flak Cannon finally started working, mowed down Tefnut.

“That’s only five,” Setback observed, accurately. “Should we go find the rest of them?”

“I will kill you in your sleep,” Visionary promised.

“What?” Bunker yelled.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: Cosmitron touched down in Megalopolis, and only Price of Freedom Wraith, Dark Watch Expatriette, and Ra were on hand to deal with its shenanigans…and by “its” I am of course referring to Megalopolis, which did way more work to cripple the heroes than the genocidal alien-tech robot did. Wraith had to use up all her Grappling Hooks just dealing with the environment, which left nothing behind for Cosmitron’s plating cards (can’t be bothered to look up the names right now), and that sure did suck having Wraith and Expatriette on the same team. The general strategy was for Wraith to tase Cosmitron, a mental image I will never stop finding funny; Expatriette to shoot it, preferably with an elemental bullet if possible, or to just shoot some drone if not possible; and for Ra to burn whatever would burn. It was a nail-biter having the team so desperately crippled, but good team communication skills and Ra being willing to blow up his staff just to change up the damage type made sure the heroes survived with HP ranging anywhere from 1 to 4.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: The Chairman was in the Final Wasteland for…reasons. He’s a murderous dictator and probably insane; I’m sure it makes sense to him if no one else. Mister Fixer, Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero, Horus, and Golem Unity decided to take care of the problem. It was okay. About the only clever thing that happened was Absolute Zero playing Sub-Zero Atmosphere to deny the Chairman one mook per round. Near the end of the game, Horus kind of screwed up Zero’s perpetual motion build with an Imbued Flame, but it just did more good than harm with Unity’s Raptor Bot and Platform Bot in play. A late-game Grease Gun made sure no one took any harm from a focused blitz to inflict about 18 HP on the Operative and 15 on the Chairman, and from there, everyone saw the writing on the wall.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Took two tries to beat basic Baron Blade with Ra: Horus, Dark Watch Nightmist, and Dark Watch Setback.

Main issue in the first game was getting damaging powers into play for Ra, getting a unlucky pool started for Setback (which seems to be a recurring issue with me playing him), and DW Nightmist simply not being able to carry the load single-handed.  They managed to flip Blade with 14 cards in the trash, but were so weakened at that point that an Elemental Redistributor and an array of Blade Battalions took them down.

Second go-round started better for the heroes.  Ra got Flaming Tornado and Staff of Ra out early.  Setback got Looking Up in play in Round 2.  Nightmist didn't start off as well, but she caught up quickly, and was essentially playing tank due to having the Amulet in play.  With more firepower bearing on Blade the heroes kept up with him, flipped him in Round 4, and then unloaded on him to finish the game by Round 7.

posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked: The Chairman again, this time going up against Freedom Plaza (I need to print off those downloaded environment cards; I’m getting sick of the ones I have). That Inspiring Presence made Nightmist’s last Oblivion spell really hurt, but it hurt the bad guys worse, so all’s well that ends well.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Matriarch and her birdies are in the Realm of Discord - harvesting apples I think.  Fought there by Absolute Zero - Elemental Wrath, Freedom Tempest, and Rook City Wraith.

Standard opening with Mask dying, and immediately coming back.  Along with a Carrion Field and fowl, fowl, and more fowl.  AZ gets a module out and starts chipping away at the Mask and the Matriarch.  Tempest plays some one-shots and then gets Cleansing Rains out since it is obviously going to be needed.  Wraith starts pouring equipment into play (thank you Impromptu Invention); she starts Stun Bolting the Matriarch and reducing fowl with Throwing Knives from her Utility Belt.  The Realm of Discord is annoying, but not amazingly so, until Time Speeeds Up.

More fowl pour out, along with both Cohort Ravens at once.  The Matriarch has DR -2, damage +2, and one raven starts eating equipment cards.  (No ongoings about due to a one-shot.)  The only thing keeping the heroes upright by then is Smoke Bombs bouncing damage around and reducing it, plus Tempest's Otherworldly Resilience.  The Realms next curveball and the one making all but low HP immune.  (yay)

Tempest finally gets Electrical Storm out and zaps a big pile of fowl.  Retaliation damage bounces among the heroes and they are all under 10 HP.  Tempest then destroys a few environment cards to get the distortions out of the way.  More knives and stun bolts at the Matriarch and the ravens trying to whittle them down to being killable.

More fowl come out and the villain deck is close to empty.  AZ shoots at the ravens (one shot for cold damage to bird, fire damage to himself - converted into cold and healing a point.)  Tempest zaps the four birds and the retaliation damage goes around.  He then Chain Lightnings the ravens and the lone remaining Carrion Field.  Plus Cleansing Rain to get the heroes some healing.  This sets up Wraith - knives drop the raven supplying DR; the next knife gets the other raven; and the third is the Matriarch's.  Followed by a Stun Bolt. 

The race is on see if they can drop her before a pile of fowl heal her up.  First card off the reshuffled villain deck is - The Mask.

Which makes things a bit anti-climatic.  Tempest has a supply of Into the Straosphere cards.  The Mask goes back on top of the villain deck for the next two rounds while the heroes pound on the Matriarch and whatever other targets come up.  (looking at you annoying Explosive Bubbles.)

Heroes win with about 6-8 HP each.
