posts.name: JimB
posts.cooked:
The Matriarch is finished. She tried to take over 1863 (it should surprise no one that a person who thinks you can take over a year is not effective at carrying out her goals), so Absolute Zero, Tempest, Unity, and Engine of War Bunker decided to take her on. In round one, Zero played a Cold Snap to make sure birds died before they could attack, because the counterattacks generally hurt less than leaving the birds in play. Tempest knocked the mask back atop the Matriarch’s and wiped out the birds, triggering a lot of evil responses from the Matriarch and a Carrion Fields, but the team sucked it up in time for Unity to get out a Bee Bot and Stealth Bot, which instantly cured almost everything I was afraid of from then on out. Bunker got out his armor, a time portal appeared to zap the Matriarch and the Carrion Fields and the Bee Bot to destroy it before it could zap any of the heavily bruised heroes. The Matriarch impotently put her mask back into play, everyone got to work on their builds except Tempest, who bitchslapped the mask back atop the deck one more time while I cackled.

Pretty standard after that. Zero had out his Focused Apertures, Tempest never got out a good power but had plenty of useful one-shots, Unity…actually struggled a bit to get a half useful card in hand, and Bunker shot everything he could. Stealth Bot didn’t last forever, but it lasted long enough to do some good while everyone, including a kindly sheriff, focused fire on the Matriarch. They got the job taken care of, though HP were getting to be a rare resource there at the end.

Also, I am pretty sure one of the bystanders was a young Alfred Hitchcock. Temporal paradox averted by fulfilling circumstance, yo.

posts.name: Oaktree
posts.cooked:
Iron Legacy is surveying locations for internment camps in the Final Wasteland when a group of heroes appear.  (GI Bunker, Eternal Haka, Ra, and DW Setback.)  Haka is annoyed at the falling property values due to IL's interest in the area.

Match #1 is a 4 round trashing of the heroes.  Ok, rematch.

Match #2 see-saws, but goes the heroes way.  Iron Legacy starts with Galvanized, Superhuman Redirection, Demoralizing Presence, and Armored Fortitude.  During the battle he added a 2nd Superhuman Redirection and Armored Fortitude.

GI Bunker works on getting an Omni-cannon shot going, some armor, and stopping the environment deck.  Plus he Panzerbusters IL every so often to help the others when IL's DR gets to -2 (and eventually -3).  Haka does some initial damage, loses his Taiha, and settles on playing Ground Pounds and drawing cards up to power a Haka of Battle.  Ra plays Drawn To The Flame and IL's DR is just enough to pull the damage under the Superhuman Redirection trigger amount.  So Ra does this or Pyre depending on IL's DR at the time, and he also uses one-shots to augment the damage.  (Ra was the one keeping IL's healing from simply being unstoppable.)  DW Setback gets Looking Up out early, and also is the only one with one-shots that can take out IL's on-going cards.  He gets one of the Superhuman Redirections early on, and takes out the other one when he has 7 HP left and 7 tokens in his unlucky pool.  Iron Legacy takes a nice shot and Setback goes down… oh wait, he played Silver Lining the turn before.

And the Ancient Library comes out.

Iron Legacy gets free of the Ground Pounds and levels Ra while he also heals 14 HP back to get up to 24 HP.  The heroes other than Ra have 7-8 HP each.  He also plays anoter On-going to inflict projectile damage on those heroes who play cards.  (Pity Ra and Drawn To the Flame are gone.)

GI Bunker Panzer-bust IL to make hero damage irreducible (IL is currently DR -3). 

Haka has a Taiha out.  He draws two more cards via Ancient Library, plays Haka of Battle - draws 2 more and then discards 12.  Taiha does 15 damage to Iron Legacy; dropping him to 9 HP.

Miss Information on a shopping trip to Megalopolis - time to purchase some diversions and some clues for a set of hapless heroes.  On her gift list this month are Legacy, Bunker, Freedom Tempest, and Golem Unity.

Diversions early and one-shots; not so many clues.  Unity loses her golems in hand.  Then everyone else loses their on-going cards.  Legacy starts playing equipment to be sacrificed and galvanizes for the others to fight diversions.  Bunker manages to keep a Flak Gun out and blasts a branch so that a stuck 'kitty kat' can fall to the ground.  Freedom Tempest ends up playing one shots for damage or utility value - like Reclaim From The Depths.  Golem Unity quickly gets some new golem cards and then rolls out Swift Bot and Stealth Bot.  Champion Bot and Cryo Bot turn up a short time later.

Some clues appear, as well as another diversion.  The bots suck up damage, and Unity feeds a Platform Bot and Raptor Bot into the fire to help kill diversions and be sacrificed.  Unity repairs bots twice to keep some in the fray.

More clues show up.  More bots die. With four clues in play Miss Information flips and the final firefight starts.  She zaps the heroes with one clue; the heroes discard cards to kill another.  Shortly afterwards Tempest Ball Lightnings the other two.  Unity is down to Champion Bot and Cryo Bot, but every time Cryo Bot gets hit he is hitting back for 3 cold damage. 

Two diversions come out.  They work over everyone and in turn get hammered by Legacy, Bunker, Tempest, and Cryo Bot.  Miss Information takes Legacy out, but she is weak enough (and the heroes have enough HP left to withstand retaliation) that Bunker's Flak Gun and a Chain Lightning from Tempest bring her down.  (Bunker at 6 HP, Tempest at 2, Unity at 3 - and no live bots.)

Ugly game against Spite in Insula Primalis using Freedom Wraith, GI Bunker, DW Setback, and DW Nightmist.  Typical in that the early stage is seeing how much damage the heroes have taken and how much equipment/ongoings they can keep deployed by the time Spite gets all five drugs out and flips.  (With a secondary challenge of whether they try and can keep any victims in the Safe House until then.)

Answer was not much equipment, and three victims.  Plus having Spite down about 10 HP by then due to Wraith giving him a few Throat Jabs under the theory that if he is not causing damage he is not healing either.

Flip-side turns into the race to wear Spite down before he finishes rubbing the heroes out a few points at a time.  The race results:

Wraith - Went down quickly due to nemesis bonus.  While she was active she was putting Stun Bolts into Spite to reduce his damage and due her part to take him down.

GI Bunker - Went down second from taking damage for using powers.  Never got an Armor Plating card to help with that.  But his consistent use of Panzer-Buster was helping with the damage the others were inflicting.

DW Setback - Helped heal the group a bit, inflicted a little damage, and lasted longer due to reduced use of powers.

DW Nightmist - Ultimate winner with *1* HP left.  Spell use got her around the toxic damage from power use.  She could also run out the Necklace and heal 4 HP a round if necessary (which essentially was how much damage Spite did to her most turns.)  A Mist-Fueled Recovery put her back near full HP once, so she could afford to cast Oblivion shots to wear Spite down, and then try to hold on while she drew cards back up (via the other hero incap abilities mainly.)  And once she got above Spite in HP the various dinos tryed to gnaw on him instead of her.

Not near as exciting as it may sound.

Finished off Miss Information on advanced mode with NM, Papa legs, Redeemer Fanatic, and Unity in Atlantis. It was a long slow slog, but they got it done.

The real story was in their first failed attempt, however. Ms. Twain opened with a Diversionary Tactics, chaining into another Diversionary Tactics, and then a Missing Resources. At the end of the first villain turn the heroes were running in circles trying to deal with a "Cat" Stuck in a Tree, an "Old Lady" in the Street, a "Diplomatic" Envoy, and a "Threat" to the President. Oh, and every one-shot in their opening hands had been discarded. They chased the "Cat" into a Phosphorescent Chamber and got so confused by all the shiny lights that they dropped even more of their stuff on the ground. They began to get a clue about their demure seceratary shortly thereafter, however, when they began to hurt even worse than before. "Oh," said Miss Information, "What Doesn't Kill You just makes you... <snigger> stronger <snicker>."

So at the end of the second villain turn (remember that that each hero had already discarded 2-3 cards at this point):

  1. Destroy 3 hero ongoing or equipment cards.
  2. The player with the most cards in play must destroy 1 of their non-character cards.
  3. Deal the 2 hero targets with the highest HP 6 melee damage each.
  4. Deal the 2 hero targets with the highest HP 5 melee damage and 5 energy damage each.
  5. Deal the 2 hero targets with the lowest HP 5 cold damage each.

Yeah, they don't really like to talk about "that one time in Atlantis." Tempest will never let them live that one down.
